4. Defendants appeared before to court of the said Assistant Judge after 1.6.88 and filed written objection against the prayer for temporary injunction denying the material allegations also contending inter alia that the suit as framed was not maintainable in law in as much as in the fact and circumstances as narrated in the suit an application u/s 50 of the Waqf Ordinance was to be filed before the Administration of Wakf or in the least in the instant suit, Administrator of Wakf should have been made part and it was further stated the no injunction njunction could be granted against admitted Mutawalli the defendant no. 4 while she was discharging her responsibility as the sitting Mutawalli. It was also alleged in the written objection that the application for temporary in junction was full of facts that are utterly false, frivolous and concocted having no hearing at all with the realities and the back ground of making the Waqf and that the Waqf in question has already been acted upon and that defendant no. 4 who was appointed as the Mutawalli as per condition in the Deed and as per law she own and possesses that suit property and as per existing law of waqf plaintiff have no right title and possession in any portion of the suit land. It was also stated in the written objection that the waqf deed was executed and registered by the waqf within the full knowledge of the plaintiff and it represents the true and genuine desire of the waqif. But the plaintiffs were not happy as the waqf did not serve their selfish interest. But so long the waqif remained alive they could not do anything and as soon as the waqif died the plaintiffs started to hatch conspiracy against the waqf as to how best get the waqi declared illegal and as such on on 7.12.80 threatened the sitting Mutawalli defendant no. 4 of dispossessing her. Hence she had to file Other Class Suit No. 1672 of 1980 in the Court of Munsif, Sherpur and on 6.7.82 obtained decree of permanent injunction in that suit restraining the defendant from entering or interfering with her possession of the suit land of waqf. It was also asserted in the written objection that the alleged waqf name registered on 1379 at the same Nalitabari Sub-Registry Office is out an out a document of forgery and a fabricated document and the same was never executed by Lal Mahmud Mondal it was also asserted in the written objection that ad-interim injunction granted earlier and ex-parte was in utter non compliance of the three essentials such as (a) the applicant must show a fair prima facie and arguable case in support of the right of claim of injunction (11) an actual or threatened violation of that right and in there should be acquiescence or delay (d) there should be greater convenience in granting then refusing injunction and equally efficacious relief must not be obtainable in any other usual mode. 

 the learned Court labouring under a misconception of law as provided in section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure passed the above order of Stay, thus committed an error of law resulting in an error in its decision occasioning failure of justice. 

 9. Mr. Saha further, submits that a dispute as to the waqf character of the property raised whether before, or alter the enrolment of the waqf, such a dispute should invariably be raised before the Administrator of Waqfs and not in the civil Court. The Waqf Ordinance being a special statute providing special procedure, it is to be availed of first in such cases. The Cognizance of the civil Court is excluded. As such, according to him, filing and continuance of the suit in the civil Court has been illegal and non est and the Assistant Judge by the impugned order committed an error resulting in an error in its decision occasioning failure of justice and the same is liable to be set aside. Mr. Saha also submits that the learned Assistant Judge was evidently wrong in staying the further proceedings of the present suit till the disposal of the subsequently instituted Miscellanies Case No. 41 of 1988 under Order, 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure the disposal of subsequently which is most uncertain. Thus keeping the temporary injunction matter pending when already there is ad-interim injunction passed ex-parte against the defendant petitioner, which is flanging overhead as a sword of democles and this is quite in Contradiction of the decree of permanent injunction earlier passed by a court of competent jurisdiction favour of the petitions in Title Suit No.1672/1980. 

 11. Heard the learned Advocate, perused the petition and considered his submissions. In the facts and circumstances, a suit for declaration at the instance of the plaintiff without making the Administrator of Waqfs a party, the learned Assistant Judge has committed an utter illegality in entertaining such a suit in the facts and circumstances, the dispute raised as to the character of the wakf property the suit could not have been filed in the Civil Court because the Waqfs Ordinance is a special statute providing special procedure and in such a case the civil Court is excluded. Where civil Court has no jurisdiction in a matter like this, I quite agree with the submission of the teamed Advocate that the entire proceedings are coram non judice. Injunction is granted when the Court is grants satisfied:- 

 I) that the applicant has a prima facie case to go to the trial 

 III) the mischief or inconvenience likely to arise from withholding injunction will be greater than which is likely the arise from granting. 

 13. Not only that the learned Assistant Judge laboring under a misconception of law as provided in section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure, by the impugned order committed a serious infraction of law resulting in an error in its decision occasioning failure of justice. Section 10 envisages two suits pending between the same parties, the subject matter being the same and the issues are also sate and in that case later suit will be stayed. In the instant case, there are not two suits but one suit and other is an application under Order 9 Rule 13 and as such the learned Assistant Judge on a sheer misconception of law and in misreading the materials on record, passed the impugned order to the great prejudice of the defendant petitioner but the same has gone very much in favour of the plaintiff opposite party most unduly. 

 16. Accordingly, the rule is made absolute. Since this is a long pending case the patties are directed to bear their own costs.
